title: Your cat's kneading is a kitten habit
topic: Why do cats knead with their paws?

lines: When your cat kneads your lap, it's acting like a nursing kitten.
Kittens push on their mother's belly with alternating paws while nursing, to get the milk flowing.

beats.text: Some even suck on blankets while they knead.
lines: But many cats never drop the habit as adults.
Some even suck on blankets while they knead.

beats.label: between paw pushes
lines: Watch closely: the paws alternate every one to two seconds, toes spreading to flash the claws, then curling up.

beats.label: purr
lines: Many cats purr while kneading, a sound kittens make mostly while newborn and feeding, a hint it's a leftover instinct.

beats.title: Kneading may also mean
lines: It may also simply feel good, like a human stretching, and it often comes right before a nap.
And since paw pads hold scent glands, after a good knead you likely walk away smelling a little like your cat.

sources.claim: Kittens knead the breast while suckling, alternating forelimbs, to stimulate lactation; cats carry this into adulthood and some suck on clothing or bedding while kneading.
The cat presses down, spreading its toes to expose its claws, then curls its toes as it lifts, alternating paws at intervals of one to two seconds.

Many cats purr while kneading; they purr mostly when newborn or feeding, supporting kneading as a remnant instinct. Kneading may feel good like a human stretching and is often a precursor to sleeping.
Cats have scent glands on the underside of their paws; when they knead people or objects, these pheromones are likely transferred.
